title: NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD CVE API 2.0)
agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology
questions: how many critical vulnerabilities were published this year
one CVE's severity score and weakness type
known exploited vulnerabilities added to the CISA catalog
vulnerabilities in a product or vendor

manual.how: Open each link in INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (each returns JSON, up to 2,000 CVEs) and save it under the given name, waiting about 6 seconds between links (NVD allows 5 requests in 30 seconds without a key). For whole years, the yearly CVE JSON 2.0 feeds at https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/data-feeds are an alternative but are large and must be filtered by hand. Upload the saved files.

cache.why: Records are re-analyzed and modified daily (lastModified); data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: NVD data are a work of the U.S. government (NIST), not subject to copyright in the U.S. (17 U.S.C. 105); the terms of use ask products that use the API to carry the notice below (https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/terms-of-use).

notices: This product uses data from the NVD API but is not endorsed or certified by the NVD.
citation: National Institute of Standards and Technology, National Vulnerability Database, {dataset}, NVD CVE API 2.0 (services.nvd.nist.gov), retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which score counts for severity: NVD's own CVSS v3.1 assessment (the default here) or the reporting organization's (CNA) score? They differ for many CVEs.
Published date or last-modified date? CVE counts by year normally use the published date.
Include CVEs still awaiting NVD analysis (no NVD score yet)? Severity counts leave them out.
